full_text_en:
Chongqing Haoyun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. v. Chongqing Jiulongpo District Xipeng Di Jing Hao Yuan Owners' Committee — Parking Space Dispute

Ruling Summary

After the completion of a residential community, as the housing units within the community are sold, the land use rights within the building area are also transferred to the owners of the community, and the land use rights in the common areas of the community belong to the owners of the community. Above-ground parking spaces that cannot be registered for property rights to become the object of ownership of a specific owner cannot become exclusive parts with exclusive rights. Such parking spaces, which occupy roads or other common areas belonging to the owners for parking motor vehicles, belong to the owners of the community.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court
(2017) Supreme People's Court Civil Retrial Application No. 2817

Retrial Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Chongqing Haoyun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. Address: Room 4-3, No. 71 Yanghe Er Village, Jiangbei District, Chongqing.

Person in Charge: Liu Anhong, General Manager of the Company.

Agent Ad Litem: Luo Zhigang, male, employee of the Company.

Respondent in Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Chongqing Jiulongpo District Xipeng Di Jing Hao Yuan Owners' Committee. Address: Inside Chongqing Jiulongpo District Xipeng Di Jing Hao Yuan Community.

Person in Charge: Xu Ermo, Director of the Owners' Committee.

The retrial applicant, Chongqing Haoyun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Haoyun Company), in connection with a parking space dispute with the respondent, Chongqing Jiulongpo District Xipeng Di Jing Hao Yuan Owners' Committee (hereinafter referred to as the Di Jing Hao Yuan Committee), being dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2016) Yu Min Zhong No. 7 of the Chongqing High People's Court, has applied to this Court for a retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to review this case, and the review has now been concluded.

Haoyun Company applied for a retrial on the following grounds: (1) The original judgment erred in the application of law. The land use right for the construction of the Di Jing Hao Yuan Community was acquired through capital contribution by Haoyun Company. Haoyun Company is the holder of the land use right. Pursuant to Article 142 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Property Law), the above-ground parking spaces planned within the building area of the Di Jing Hao Yuan Community should belong to Haoyun Company. The original judgment, instead of applying Article 142 of the Property Law, applied Article 63(2) of the Chongqing Property Management Regulations, which constitutes an error in the application of law. (2) The original judgment found that the parking spaces in question were spaces occupying roads or other common areas belonging to the owners, which lacks factual basis. The green area, common area, and traffic roads of the community had been accepted as up to standard by the relevant government departments and were filed for reference. The green area of the community even exceeded the planned area, so there was no situation of occupying any common area. Accordingly, Haoyun Company applied for a retrial under Article 200(2) and (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The Di Jing Hao Yuan Committee submitted comments, stating that the parking spaces in question belong to the owners of the community, and Haoyun Company has no rights to them. (1) The parking spaces in question use the land use rights that are commonly owned by all owners. After Haoyun Company handled the initial registration and transfer registration of the housing units for the owners of the community, the owners jointly enjoy the entire land use right of the community. Pursuant to Article 74(3) of the Property Law, if parking spaces occupy roads or common areas belonging to the owners, the parking spaces should belong to the owners. (2) Haoyun Company cannot obtain the title certificate for the parking spaces in question. The parking spaces in question are not exclusive parts, and the property rights should belong to all owners of the community. (3) The parking spaces in question were not included in the floor area ratio and did not participate in the allocation of planned construction land area, so the property rights should belong to the owners.

Upon review, this Court finds that the issues in this case are: (1) whether the application of law by the original judgment is indeed erroneous; and (2) whether the basic facts found in the original judgment lack evidentiary support.

(1) Whether the application of law by the original judgment is indeed erroneous

Haoyun Company, in its retrial application, contended that the original judgment erred in the application of law, arguing that Article 142 of the Property Law should have been applied instead of Article 63(2) of the Chongqing Property Management Regulations. Article 142 of the Property Law provides: "The ownership of buildings, structures, and their ancillary facilities constructed by the holder of the construction land use right belongs to the holder of the construction land use right, unless there is evidence to the contrary." Meanwhile, Article 63(2) of the Chongqing Property Management Regulations provides: "After an construction unit has lawfully obtained the registration of property rights for parking spaces and garages, it may sell the parking spaces and garages to the owners. When the number of parking spaces and garages to be sold is equal to or less than the number of housing units in the property management area, each owner may only purchase one parking space or garage." The two provisions are not contradictory. Since Haoyun Company sold the housing units to the owners of the community, the land use rights within the community also transferred to the owners of the community, and the land use rights in the common areas of the community belong to the owners of the community. Therefore, Haoyun Company's assertion that the above-ground parking spaces in question should belong to it by applying Article 142 of the Property Law cannot be sustained. The original judgment applied Article 63(2) of the Chongqing Property Management Regulations for the purpose of clarifying that a construction unit can only sell parking spaces or garages after having obtained the registration of property rights for them. Since the parking spaces in question cannot obtain property rights registration, they cannot be sold. Therefore, the original judgment's application of Article 63(2) of the Chongqing Property Management Regulations was not improper. Haoyun Company's ground for retrial that the original judgment erred in the application of law cannot be established, and this Court does not support it.

(2) Whether the basic facts found in the original judgment lack evidentiary support

Pursuant to Article 2(1) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in Hearing Disputes over Building Ownership Distinction, which provides: "Housing units, parking spaces, stalls, and other specific spaces within a building area that meet the following conditions shall be deemed as exclusive parts as referred to in Chapter 6 of the Property Law: (1) having structural independence and being clearly distinguishable; (2) having functional independence and being capable of exclusive use; and (3) being capable of being registered as the object of ownership of a specific owner." The parking spaces in question cannot undergo property rights registration, and therefore cannot become exclusive parts with exclusive rights. Even if Haoyun Company paid the construction land use right transfer fee for the building area when constructing the Di Jing Hao Yuan Community and became the holder of the construction land use right, after the completion of the community, with the sale of the housing units within the community, the land use rights within the building area of the community also transferred, and the land use rights in the common areas of the community belong to the owners of the community. Since the parking spaces in question cannot undergo property rights registration and cannot become exclusive parts, the original judgment's determination that such parking spaces constitute spaces occupying roads or other common areas belonging to the owners for parking motor vehicles is not improper. The developer's obligation to have the community it built pass acceptance inspection is a basic obligation, and whether the green area exceeds the planned area has no necessary connection to the determination of whether the parking spaces occupy common areas belonging to the owners. Therefore, Haoyun Company's ground for retrial that the original judgment's finding that the parking spaces in question were spaces occupying roads or other common areas belonging to the owners lacked factual basis cannot be established.

In conclusion, Haoyun Company's application for retrial does not meet the circumstances provided in Article 200(2) and (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 204(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 395(2) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

The application for retrial of Chongqing Haoyun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. is dismissed.

Judge: Wang Jijun
